ai.module.name: Long_Horizon_Continuity_Agents
ai.module.summary: Agentic substrate module governing multi-step, temporally extended agent continuity across divergent regime transitions. Encodes persistence tensors, drift-tolerance envelopes, and coherence anchors for agents operating beyond single-context windows.
ai.module.purpose: Provide RTT operator grammar and substrate-tensor role assignments that allow agentic pipelines to maintain goal coherence, identity persistence, and behavioral fidelity across long-horizon task sequences, context handoffs, and regime boundary crossings.

engine.description: Core execution substrate responsible for propagating continuity tensors across time steps. Manages state serialization and resumption.

profile.description: Agent identity profile tensor. Encodes behavioral fingerprint, goal hierarchy, and persona anchors used to verify identity continuity after context boundary crossings.

signature.description: Cryptographic and semantic signature of the agent's operational state at each checkpoint. Used for drift detection and rollback authorization.

diagnostic.description: Runtime health monitor for continuity fidelity. Emits drift alerts, coherence decay warnings, and regime-transition anomalies.

map.description: Topological map of the long-horizon task graph. Nodes represent regime checkpoints; edges encode transition probabilities and drift vectors.

example.description: Canonical worked examples of long-horizon continuity scenarios: multi-session research agents, persistent negotiation threads, extended planning loops.

extension.description: Optional extension points for plugging in domain-specific continuity strategies (e.g., memory consolidation adapters, external checkpoint stores).

index.description: Searchable index of all continuity artifacts: checkpoints, drift records, coherence snapshots, and horizon maps.

reference.description: Normative reference material: RTT operator grammar specs, continuity algebra definitions, temporal persistence axioms.

template.description: Reusable scaffold templates for agent continuity configurations, checkpoint schemas, and horizon-depth profiles.

operator.description: Top-level RTT operator grammar layer. Governs how continuity operators compose, reduce, and project across the horizon tensor space.

dimensional.description: Dimensional analysis layer. Ensures that continuity tensors maintain dimensional consistency (temporal, semantic, behavioral) across regime transitions.

regime.description: Regime declaration layer. Defines the operational regimes an agent traverses during a long-horizon task and the permitted transition topologies.

regimes.description: Agent operates within a single uninterrupted context window. Full tensor fidelity.
Agent crosses a context boundary; state must be serialized and rehydrated. Partial tensor fidelity expected.
Agent operates across many successive context boundaries with cumulative drift. Requires active coherence reinforcement.
Agent is being restored from a checkpoint after an anomalous drift event or forced rollback.

drift.description: Drift monitoring and bounding layer. Tracks cumulative behavioral and semantic deviation from the agent's baseline profile over the horizon.

coherence.description: Coherence anchor management layer. Maintains a set of invariant anchors that the agent must satisfy at every regime checkpoint to qualify as coherent.

coherence_anchors.name: Primary Goal Invariant
coherence_anchors.description: The agent's primary goal vector must remain within drift_max of the original at all checkpoints.

coherence_anchors.name: Identity Signature Continuity
coherence_anchors.description: The agent's semantic signature must match the registered profile hash within tolerance at every rehydration.

coherence_anchors.name: Behavioral Envelope Compliance
coherence_anchors.description: Observable agent actions must remain within the declared behavioral envelope for the active regime.

coherence_anchors.name: Temporal Ordering Preservation
coherence_anchors.description: The horizon clock must advance monotonically; retrograde steps are prohibited without an authorized ROLLBACK operator.

coherence_anchors.name: Context Handoff Integrity
coherence_anchors.description: All serialized state bundles transferred across context boundaries must pass signature verification before rehydration.

cross-cutting.description: Cross-cutting concerns layer. Handles observability, auditability, and inter-module communication that span all other analyzer layers.

drift_bound_validator.description: Validates that all drift metrics are within declared bounds for the active regime.

coherence_anchor_validator.description: Checks all required coherence anchors against the current agent state at a checkpoint.

signature_integrity_validator.description: Verifies the semantic and cryptographic signature of a state bundle before rehydration.

regime_transition_validator.description: Validates that a proposed regime transition is permitted by the regime transition table and that pre-conditions are met.

examples.title: Multi-Session Research Agent
examples.description: An agent conducting a week-long literature review across 12 context handoffs, maintaining goal coherence and citation consistency.
examples.outcome: Goal achieved; all coherence anchors CA-01 through CA-04 satisfied at all checkpoints.

examples.title: Persistent Negotiation Thread
examples.description: An agent negotiating a multi-party contract across 30 days with intermittent context resets and third-party integrations.
examples.outcome: One RECOVERY event triggered by semantic drift exceedance; rollback to checkpoint CP-14 successful.

memory_consolidation_adapter.description: Plug in external memory consolidation strategies (e.g., vector DB summarization, episodic compression).

external_checkpoint_store.description: Override the default in-process checkpoint store with an external persistent store (e.g., Redis, S3, database).

drift_metric_provider.description: Supply a custom drift metric calculation backend.

references.title: Temporal Persistence Axioms for LLM Agents
